p200.zh: 访问这个网站看预告片"内幕乔布",一部探索现代金融危机的电影.

p201.original: The Median Average Sales Price for New Single-Family Homes, 1990–2015
p201.zh: 1990-2015年新家庭平均销售价格中位数

p202.original: Investors can also put money into other tangible assets such as gold, silver, and other precious metals, or in duller commodities like sugar, cocoa, coffee, orange juice, oil, and natural gas. The return on these investments derives from the saver’s hope of buying low, selling high, and receiving a capital gain. Investing in, say, gold or coffee offers relatively little in the way of nonfinancial benefits to the user (unless the investor likes to caress gold or gaze upon a warehouse full of coffee). Typically, investors in these commodities never even see the physical good. Instead, they sign a contract that takes ownership of a certain quantity of these commodities, which are stored in a warehouse, and later they sell the ownership to someone else. As one example, from 1981 to 2005, the gold prices generally fluctuated between about $300 and $500 per ounce, but then rose sharply to over $1,100 per ounce by early 2010. In January 2017, prices were hovering around $1,191 per ounce, and they have since increased, reaching over $1,900 by early 2022.
p202.zh: 投资者还可以将资金投入其他有形资产,如金、银和其他贵金属,或者投入糖、可可、咖啡、橙汁、石油和天然气等较乏味的商品。 这些投资的收益来自储蓄者购买低价、出售高价和获得资本收益的希望。投资黄金或咖啡对用户的非金融利益来说相对来说很少(除非投资者喜欢抚摸黄金或凝视满满咖啡的仓库).一般来说,这些商品的投资者甚至从未看到过实物价值。 相反,他们签署了一份合同,将一定数量的这些商品的所有权收归仓库,后来又将所有权卖给别人。 例如,从1981年到2005年,黄金价格一般在每盎司300美元到500美元之间波动,但到2010年初,则急剧上涨到每盎司1 100美元以上。2017年1月,价格徘徊在每盎司1,191美元左右,此后涨幅不断,到2022年初达到1,900美元以上.

p203.original: A final area of tangible assets consists of “collectibles” like paintings, fine wine, jewelry, antiques, or even baseball cards. Most collectibles provide returns both in the form of services or of a potentially higher selling price in the future. You can use paintings by hanging them on the wall; jewelry by wearing it; baseball cards by displaying them. You can also hope to sell them someday for more than you paid for them. However, the evidence on prices of collectibles, while scanty, is that while they may go through periods where prices skyrocket for a time, you should not expect to make a higher-than-average rate of return over a sustained period of time from investing in this way.
p203.zh: 有形资产的最后领域包括绘画、精美酒、珠宝、古董、甚至棒球卡等“收藏品”。 大多数可收取货款既以服务形式提供,也以未来可能较高的销售价格提供回报。 你可以使用绘画,将画挂在墙上;珠宝可以佩戴;棒球卡可以展示. 你也可以希望有一天能卖掉它们 价格比你付的钱还多 然而,关于可收货价格的证据虽然很少,但表明,虽然这些价格可能经历了价格一度暴涨的时期,但人们不应指望在持续一段时间内从这种投资中获得高于平均的收益率。

p204.original: The bottom line on investing in tangible assets: rate of return—moderate, especially if you can receive nonfinancial benefits from, for example, living in the house; risk—moderate for housing or high if you buy gold or baseball cards; liquidity—low, because it often takes considerable time and energy to sell a house or a piece of fine art and turn your capital gain into cash. The next Clear It Up feature explains the issues in the recent U.S. housing market crisis.
p204.zh: 关于有形资产投资的底线:回报率——中度,特别是如果能够从住房中获取非财政利益;风险——如果购买金牌或棒球卡,住房或高额住房的中度;流动性低,因为出售房屋或精美艺术品,将资本收益转化为现金往往需要相当的时间和精力。接下来的Clear It Up 特性解释了美国最近住房市场危机中的问题.

p205.original: What was all the commotion in the recent U.S. housing market?
p205.zh: 最近的美国住房市场里 究竟有什么骚乱?

p206.original: The cumulative average annual growth rate in housing prices from 1981 to 2000 was 5.1%. The price of an average U.S. home then took off from 2003 to 2005, rising more than 10% per year. No serious analyst believed this rate of growth was sustainable; after all, if housing prices grew at, say, 11% per year over time, the average price of a home would more than double every seven years. However, at the time many serious analysts saw no reason for deep concern. After all, housing prices often change in fits and starts, like all prices, and a price surge for a few years is often followed by prices that are flat or even declining a bit as local markets adjust.
p206.zh: 1981年至2000年,住房价格年均累计增长率为5.1%。之后,美国平均住宅的价格从2003年到2005年上涨了10%以上。没有一个严肃的分析家认为这一增长率是可持续的;毕竟,如果住房价格逐年上涨11%,那么住房的平均价格每7年将增加一倍以上。 然而,当时许多认真的分析家认为没有理由深感关切。毕竟,房价经常像所有价格一样在适应和起步上发生变化,几年来价格暴涨之后,往往会随着当地市场的调整而出现扁平甚至下降。

p207.original: The sharp rise in housing prices was driven by a high level of demand for housing. Interest rates were low, so financial institutions encouraged people to borrow money to buy a house. Banks became much more flexible in their lending, making what were called “subprime” loans. Banks loaned money with low, or sometimes no down payment. They offered loans with very low payments for the first two years, but then much higher payments after that. The idea was that housing prices would keep rising, so the borrower would just refinance the mortgage two years in the future, and thus would not ever have to make the higher payments. Some banks even offered so-called NINJA loans, which meant a financial institution issued a loan even though the borrower had no income, no job, nor assets.
p207.zh: 住房价格的急剧上涨是住房需求高的原因。利率很低,所以金融机构鼓励人们借钱购买房屋.银行在贷款方面变得更加灵活,提供了所谓的“次级”贷款。银行贷款数额很低,有时甚至没有定金。 他们提供贷款,头两年的付款非常低,但之后付款要高得多。想法是房价会持续上涨,因此借款人会只是在未来两年重新为抵押贷款融资,因此再也不需要支付更高的价钱. 一些银行甚至提供所谓的NINJA贷款,这意味着一个金融机构发放贷款,尽管借款人没有收入,没有工作,也没有资产.

p208.original: In retrospect, these loans seem outlandish. Many borrowers figured, however, that as long as housing prices kept rising, it made sense to buy. Many lenders used a process called “securitizing,” in which they sold their mortgages to financial companies, which put all the mortgages into a big pool, creating large financial securities, and then re-sold these mortgage-backed securities to investors. In this way, the lenders off-loaded the mortgage risks to investors. Investors were interested in mortgage-backed securities as they appeared to offer a steady stream of income, provided the borrowers repaid them. Investors relied on the ratings agencies to assess the credit risk associated with the mortgage-backed securities. In hindsight, it appears that the credit agencies were far too lenient in their ratings of many of the securitized loans. Bank and financial regulators watched the steady rise in the market for mortgage-backed securities, but saw no reason at the time to intervene.
p208.zh: 回顾过去,这些贷款似乎无利可图。 然而,许多借款人认为,只要房价持续上涨,购买就是合理的。 许多放款人使用一种称为“证券化”的程序,将抵押权出售给金融公司,将所有抵押权放入一个大集合,形成大型金融证券,然后将这些抵押支持的证券重新卖给投资者。 通过这种方式,放款人将抵押风险从投资者身上卸下。投资者对抵押支持的证券感兴趣,因为他们似乎提供稳定的收入流,只要借款人偿还。投资者依靠评级机构评估与抵押担保有关的信用风险。事后看来,信贷机构对许多证券化贷款的评级似乎过于宽松。银行和金融监管者观察了抵押担保证券市场稳步上升,但认为当时没有理由进行干预。

p209.original: When housing prices turned down, many households that had borrowed when prices were high found that what they owed the bank was more than what their home was worth. Many banks believed that they had diversified by selling their individual loans and instead buying securities based on mortgage loans from all over the country. After all, banks thought back in 2005, the average house price had not declined at any time since the Great Depression in the 1930s. These securities based on mortgage loans, however, turned out to be far riskier than expected. The bust in housing prices weakened both bank and household finances, and thus helped bring on the 2008–2009 Great Recession.
p209.zh: 当房价回落时,许多在高价时借过钱的家庭发现,他们欠银行的钱比他们的房子值多. 许多银行认为,它们通过出售个人贷款而实现了多样化,而是以来自全国各地的抵押贷款为基础购买证券。毕竟,银行在2005年回想起,自20世纪30年代大萧条以来,平均房价从未下降过. 然而,这些基于抵押贷款的证券的风险远高于预期。房价暴跌削弱了银行和家庭财政,从而促成了2008-2009年的大衰退。

p210.original: The Tradeoffs between Return and Risk
p210.zh: 回归与风险之间的权衡

p211.original: The discussion of financial investments has emphasized the expected rate of return, the risk, and the liquidity of each investment.  summarizes these characteristics.
p211.zh: 关于金融投资的讨论强调了每项投资的预期收益率、风险和流动性。

p220.zh: 非常高,非常高,非常高,非常高,非常高,非常高

p253.original: The household investment choices listed here display a tradeoff between the expected return and the degree of risk involved. Bank accounts have very low risk and very low returns; bonds have higher risk but higher returns; and stocks are riskiest of all but have the potential for still higher returns. In effect, the higher average return compensates for the higher degree of risk. If risky assets like stocks did not also offer a higher average return, then few investors would want them.
p253.zh: 此处列出的家庭投资选择表明,预期收益与所涉风险程度之间有权衡。银行帐户的风险非常低,收益非常低;债券的风险较高,但收益较高;股票风险最大,但仍有可能获得更高的收益。 实际上,较高的平均收益补偿了较高的风险程度。 如果股票等风险资产不也能提供较高的平均收益,那么投资者就很少想要这些资产。

p254.original: This tradeoff between return and risk complicates the task of any financial investor: Is it better to invest safely or to take a risk and go for the high return? Ultimately, choices about risk and return will be based on personal preferences. However, it is often useful to examine risk and return in the context of different time frames.
p254.zh: 回报与风险之间的这种权衡使任何金融投资人的任务复杂化:安全投资还是承担风险并争取高回报更好?归根结底,关于风险和回报的选择将基于个人偏好。 然而,在不同的时间范围内审查风险和回报往往是有益的。

p255.original: The high returns of stock market investments refer to a high average return that we can expect over a period of several years or decades. The high risk of such investments refers to the fact that in shorter time frames, from months to a few years, the rate of return may fluctuate a great deal. Thus, a person near retirement age, who already owns a house, may prefer reduced risk and certainty about retirement income. For young workers, just starting to make a reasonably profitable living, it may make sense to put most of their savings for retirement in mutual funds. Mutual funds are able to take advantage of their buying and selling size and thereby reduce transaction costs for investors. Stocks are risky in the short term, to be sure, but when the worker can look forward to several decades during which stock market ups and downs can even out, stocks will typically pay a much higher return over that extended period than will bonds or bank accounts. Thus, one must consider tradeoffs between risk and return in the context of where the investor is in life.
p255.zh: 股票市场投资的高回报率是指我们可以预期在数年或数十年的时间内实现的高平均回报率. 这种投资的高风险是指在较短的时间内,从几个月到几年,收益率可能波动很大。 因此,已经拥有住房的接近退休年龄的人可能倾向于降低退休收入的风险和确定性。 对年轻工人来说,刚刚开始有合理利润的生活,把他们的大部分储蓄用共同基金退休是有意义的。共同基金能够利用它们的买卖规模,从而降低投资者的交易成本。短期内,股票风险很大,但当工人可以期待数十年股票市场上下波动甚至可以退出时,股票在很长一段时间内通常比债券或银行账户支付高得多的收益。 因此,在投资者生活的背景下,必须考虑风险与回报之间的权衡。

p257.original: We can categorize all investments according to three key characteristics: average expected return, degree of risk, and liquidity. To obtain a higher rate of return, an investor must typically accept either more risk or less liquidity. Banks are an example of a financial intermediary, an institution that operates to coordinate supply and demand in the financial capital market. Banks offer a range of accounts, including checking accounts, savings accounts, and certificates of deposit. Under the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), banks purchase insurance against the risk of a bank failure.
p257.zh: 我们可以按照三个关键特征对所有投资进行分类:平均预期收益、风险程度和流动性。 为了获得更高的回报率,投资者通常必须接受更多的风险或更少的流动性。银行是金融中介机构的一个范例,该机构负责协调金融资本市场的供求。银行提供各种账户,包括检查账户、储蓄账户和存款证明。 在联邦存款保险公司(FDIC)下,银行购买银行倒闭风险保险.

p258.original: A typical bond promises the financial investor a series of payments over time, based on the interest rate at the time the financial institution issues the bond, and when the borrower repays it. Bonds that offer a high rate of return but also a relatively high chance of defaulting on the payments are called high-yield or junk bonds. The bond yield is the rate of return that a bond promises to pay at the time of purchase. Even when bonds make payments based on a fixed interest rate, they are somewhat risky, because if interest rates rise for the economy as a whole, an investor who owns bonds issued at lower interest rates is now locked into the low rate and suffers a loss.
p258.zh: 典型的债券承诺金融投资人随时间推移进行一系列的支付,其基础是金融机构发行债券时的利率,以及借款人偿还债券时的利率.提供高回报率但也有较高的拖欠付款机会的债券称为高收益债券或垃圾债券。债券收益率是债券在购买时承诺支付的回报率. 即使债券以固定利率支付,它们也有一定的风险,因为如果整个经济的利率上升,那么拥有低利率发行的债券的投资者现在被锁定在低利率中,并遭受损失.

p259.original: Changes in the stock price depend on changes in expectations about future profits. Investing in any individual firm is somewhat risky, so investors are wise to practice diversification, which means investing in a range of companies. A mutual fund purchases an array of stocks and/or bonds. An investor in the mutual fund then receives a return depending on the fund's overall performance as a whole. A mutual fund that seeks to imitate the overall behavior of the stock market is called an index fund.
p259.zh: 股票价格的变化取决于对未来利润的预期的变化.对任何个别公司进行投资都有些风险,因此投资者明智地实行多样化,这意味着对一系列公司进行投资。共同基金购买一系列股票和(或)债券。共同基金的投资人然后根据基金的整体业绩获得回报。 一个共同基金试图模仿股票市场的整体行为,称为指数基金.

p260.original: We can also regard housing and other tangible assets as forms of financial investment, which pay a rate of return in the form of capital gains. Housing can also offer a nonfinancial return—specifically, you can live in it.
p260.zh: 我们还可将住房和其他有形资产视为金融投资的形式,以资本收益的形式支付收益率。住房还可以提供非经济回报,具体来说,你可以住在住房中。

p262.original:
Calculate the equity each of these people has in their home:
  Eva just bought a house for $200,000 by putting 10% as a down payment and borrowing the rest from the bank.
Freda bought a house for $150,000 in cash, but if she were to sell it now, it would sell for $250,000.
Ben bought a house for $100,000. He put 20% down and borrowed the rest from the bank. However, the value of the house has now increased to $160,000 and he has paid off $20,000 of the bank loan.
p262.zh: 计算这些人在家中的股本:伊娃刚以20万美元买下一栋房子,将10%作为首付,其余部分从银行借款.佛瑞达以15万元现金买下一栋房子,但如果现在卖掉的话,这栋房子会卖出25万元. 本以十万元买房. 他放下了20%,从银行借了剩下的钱. 然而,该房屋的价值现已增加到160,000美元,他已经支付了银行贷款的20,000美元.

p263.original: Remember, equity is the market value of the house minus what is still owed to the bank. Thus: the value of the house is $200,000, Fred owes $180,000 to the bank, and his equity is $20,000.
p263.zh: 记住,股本是房子的市值减去仍欠银行的金额. 因此:房子价值为20万美元,弗雷德欠银行18万美元,他的股本为2万美元.

p264.original: The value of Freda’s house is $250,000. It does not matter what price she bought it for. She owes zero to the bank, so her equity is the whole $250,000.
p264.zh: Freda的房屋价值为25万美元. 她买它要多少钱并不重要 她欠银行零,所以她的股本是25万元

p265.original: The value of Frank’s house is $160,000. He owes $60,000 to the bank (the original $80,000 minus the $20,000 he has paid off the loan). His equity is $100,000.
p265.zh: 弗兰克的房屋价值为16万美元. 他欠银行6万元(原8万元减去他已经还清贷款的2万元). 他的股本是10万元.

p266.original: Which has a higher average return over time: stocks, bonds, or a savings account? Explain your answer.
p266.zh: 长期平均收益较高的哪一个:股票、债券或储蓄账户?解释你的答案。

p267.original: Over a sustained period of time, stocks have an average return higher than bonds, and bonds have an average return higher than a savings account. This is because in any given year the value of a savings account changes very little. In contrast, stock values can grow or decline by a very large amount (for example, the S&P 500 increased 26% in 2009 after declining 37% in 2008. The value of a bond, which depends largely on interest rate fluctuations, varies far less than a stock, but more than a savings account.
p267.zh: 在一个持续时期内,股票的平均收益高于债券,债券的平均收益高于储蓄账户。这是因为在任何一年,储蓄账户的价值变化很小。相比之下,股票价值可能增长或下降幅度非常大(例如,2009年,S&P 500在2008年下降37%之后增加了26%)。债券的价值主要取决于利率波动,其差异远远小于股票,但大于储蓄账户。

p268.original: Investors sometimes fear that a high-risk investment is especially likely to have low returns. Is this fear true? Does a high risk mean the return must be low?
p268.zh: 投资者有时担心高风险投资特别可能回报低。 这是真的吗?高风险是否意味着回报率一定很低?

p269.original: When people believe that a high-risk investment must have a low return, they are getting confused between what risk and return mean. Yes, a high-risk investment might have a low return, but it might also have a high return. Risk refers to the fact that a wide range of outcomes is possible. However, a high-risk investment must, on average, expect a relatively high return or else no one would be willing to take the risk. Thus, it is quite possible—even likely—for an investment to have high risk and high return. Indeed, the reason that an investment has a high expected return is that it also has a high risk.
p269.zh: 当人们相信高风险投资的回报率一定很低时,他们就会混淆风险和回报的含义. 是的,高风险投资可能回报率低,但也可能回报率高。风险是指可以取得广泛成果这一事实。 然而,高风险投资平均必须期望较高的回报,否则就没有人愿意承担风险。 因此,一项投资很可能——甚至有可能——具有很高的风险和高回报。 事实上,投资的预期回报率高的原因是,投资的风险也很高。

p271.zh: 为什么银行被称为“金融中介机构”?

p272.original: Name several different kinds of bank account. How are they different?
p272.zh: 列出几种不同的银行账户。 他们有什么不同?

p293.original: Getting rich may seem straightforward enough. Figure out what companies are going to grow and earn high profits in the future, or figure out what companies are going to become popular for everyone else to buy. Those companies are the ones that will pay high dividends or whose stock price will climb in the future. Then, buy stock in those companies. Presto! Multiply your money!
p293.zh: 发财似乎足够直截了当了找出未来哪些公司会增长,赚取高利润,或者找出哪些公司会成为其他人购买的热门企业. 这些公司将支付高额股利,或其股票价格将在未来攀升。 然后,买这些公司的股票。普莱斯托! Presto!赚你的钱!

p294.original: Why is this path to riches not as easy as it sounds? This module first discusses the problems with picking stocks, and then discusses a more reliable but undeniably duller method of accumulating personal wealth.
p294.zh: 为什么这条通往财富的道路没有听起来那么容易呢? 这个单元首先讨论采摘股票的问题,然后讨论一种比较可靠但不可否认是较乏味的积累个人财富的方法。

p295.original: Why It Is Hard to Get Rich Quick: The Random Walk Theory
p295.zh: 为什么很难快速获得财富:随机行走理论

p296.original: The chief problem with attempting to buy stock in companies that will have higher prices in the future is that many other financial investors are trying to do the same thing. Thus, in attempting to get rich in the stock market, it is no help to identify a company that is going to earn high profits if many other investors have already reached the same conclusion, because the stock price will already be high, based on the expected high level of future profits.
p296.zh: 试图在将来价格较高的公司购买股票的主要问题是,许多其他金融投资者也在试图这样做。 因此,在试图在股票市场上发财时,如果其他许多投资者已经得出同样的结论,那么确定一个将要赚取高利润的公司是无济于事的,因为股票价格已经很高,基于预期未来高利润水平.

p297.original: The idea that stock prices are based on expectations about the future has a powerful and unexpected implication. If expectations determine stock price, then shifts in expectations will determine shifts in the stock price. Thus, what matters for predicting whether the stock price of a company will do well is not whether the company will actually earn profits in the future. Instead, you must find a company that analysts widely believe at present to have poor prospects, but that will actually turn out to be a shining star. Brigades of stock market analysts and individual investors are carrying out such research 24 hours a day.
p297.zh: 股价以对未来的预期为根据的观念,具有强大和意想不到的影响. 如果预期决定股票价格,那么预期的变动会决定股票价格的变动. 因此,预测公司股票价格是否会好起来的关键不是公司将来是否真的能赚取利润. 相反,你必须找到一个公司, 分析家们现在普遍认为, 前景不佳, 但实际上,这将会变成一个闪耀的明星。股票市场分析员和个别投资者的队伍每天24小时进行这种研究。

p298.original: The fundamental problem with predicting future stock winners is that, by definition, no one can predict the future news that alters expectations about profits. Because stock prices will shift in response to unpredictable future news, these prices will tend to follow what mathematicians call a “random walk with a trend.” The “random walk” part means that, on any given day, stock prices are just as likely to rise as to fall. “With a trend” means that over time, the upward steps tend to be larger than the downward steps, so stocks do gradually climb.
p298.zh: 预测未来股票赢家的根本问题是,顾名思义,没有人能预测未来会改变对利润的预期的消息. 因为股票价格会随着未来无法预测的消息而变化,这些价格往往会跟随数学家所谓的“随趋势而行的狂暴 ” 。 “随机走”部分意味着,在任何特定的日子里,股票价格都有可能上涨,甚至下跌。" 有趋势 " 意味着随着时间推移,向上阶梯往往大于向下阶梯,因此种群的确逐渐攀升.

p299.original: If stocks follow a random walk, then not even financial professionals will be able to choose those that will beat the average consistently. While some investment advisers are better than average in any given year, and some even succeed for a number of years in a row, the majority of financial investors do not outguess the market. If we look back over time, it is typically true that half or two-thirds of the mutual funds that attempted to pick stocks which would rise more than the market average actually ended up performing worse than the market average. For the average investor who reads the newspaper business pages over a cup of coffee in the morning, the odds of doing better than full-time professionals is not very good at all. Trying to pick the stocks that will gain a great deal in the future is a risky and unlikely way to become rich.
p299.zh: 如果股票是随机走过的,那么,即使是财务专业人员也无法选择一贯高于平均数的股票。 虽然有些投资顾问在任何一年中都比平均水平好,有些甚至连续数年成功,但大多数金融投资者并不超越市场。 如果我们回顾过去,通常情况是,试图购买股票的半数或三分之二的共同基金实际上比市场平均水平上升得更严重,结果却比市场平均水平差。 对于早上在咖啡杯上阅读报纸商业版面的普通投资者来说,比全职专业人员做得更好的几率根本不是那么好.试图挑选将来将获得巨大收益的股票,是冒险的,不可能成为富人的方法.

p300.original: Getting Rich the Slow, Boring Way

p301.original: Many U.S. citizens can accumulate a large amount of wealth during their lifetimes, if they make two key choices. The first is to complete additional education and training. In 2020, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported median weekly usual earnings for full-time wage and salary workers age 25 and over that corresponded to annual income of $40,612 for those with a high school diploma, $48,776 for those with a two-year associate degree, and $67,860 for those with a four-year bachelor’s degree. Learning is not only good for you, but it pays off financially, too.

p321.original: How Capital Markets Transform Financial Flows
p321.zh: 资本市场如何改变资金流动

p322.original: Financial capital markets have the power to repackage money as it moves from those who supply financial capital to those who demand it. Banks accept checking account deposits and turn them into long-term loans to companies. Individual firms sell shares of stock and issue bonds to raise capital. Firms make and sell an astonishing array of goods and services, but an investor can receive a return on the company’s decisions by buying stock in that company. Financial investors sell and resell stocks and bonds to one another. Venture capitalists and angel investors search for promising small companies. Mutual funds combine the stocks and bonds—and thus, indirectly, the products and investments—of many different companies.
p322.zh: 金融资本市场有权重新包装资金,因为资金从提供金融资本的人转移到需求者。银行接受支票账户存款,将其转为对公司的长期贷款.个别公司出售股票股份,发行债券以筹集资本.公司制造和销售一系列惊人的商品和服务,但投资者可以通过购买该公司的股票获得公司决定的回报。金融投资者互相出售和转售股票和债券.风险资本家和天使投资者寻找有前途的小公司。共同基金将许多不同公司的股票和债券——从而间接地将产品和投资——结合起来。

Financial markets are society’s mechanisms for bringing together these forces of demand and supply.

p325.original: The Housing Bubble and the Financial Crisis of 2007

p326.original: The housing boom and bust in the United States, and the resulting multi-trillion-dollar decline in home equity, began with the fall of home prices starting in 2007. As home values dipped, many home prices fell below the amount the borrower owed on the mortgage and owners stopped paying and defaulted on their loan. Banks found that their assets (loans) became worthless. Many financial institutions around the world had invested in mortgage-backed securities, or had purchased insurance on mortgage-backed securities. When housing prices collapsed, the value of those financial assets collapsed as well. The asset side of the banks’ balance sheets dropped, causing bank failures and bank runs. Around the globe, financial institutions were bankrupted or nearly so. The result was a large decrease in lending and borrowing, or a freezing up of available credit. When credit dries up, the economy is on its knees. The crisis was not limited to the United States. Iceland, Ireland, the United Kingdom, Spain, Portugal, and Greece all had similar housing boom and bust cycles, and similar credit freezes.
p326.zh: 美国的房屋繁荣和崩盘,以及由此导致的房屋股本的多亿-美元下跌,始于2007年开始的房价下跌. 由于住房价值下降,许多住房价格低于借款人所欠抵押贷款的数额,房主停止支付贷款并违约。银行发现其资产(贷款)已无价值。全世界许多金融机构都投资于抵押担保,或购买了抵押担保的保险。 当住房价格暴跌时,这些金融资产的价值也崩溃。银行资产负债表的资产方面下降,导致银行倒闭和银行运转。 全球各地的金融机构几乎破产。 结果,贷款和借款大幅度减少,或现有信贷被冻结。 当信贷枯竭时,经济就会跪在地上。危机不仅限于美国。冰岛、爱尔兰、联合王国、西班牙、葡萄牙和希腊的住房繁荣和萧条周期都类似,信贷冻结也类似。

p327.original: If businesses cannot access financial capital, they cannot make physical capital investments. Those investments ultimately lead to job creation. When credit dried up, businesses invested less, and they ultimately laid off millions of workers. This caused incomes to drop, which caused demand to drop. In turn businesses sold less, so they laid off more workers. Compounding these events, as economic conditions worsened, financial institutions were even less likely to make loans.
p327.zh: 如果企业无法获得金融资本,它们就不能进行实物资本投资。 这些投资最终导致创造就业机会。 当信贷枯竭时,企业投资减少,最终解雇了数百万工人。 这导致收入下降,导致需求下降。反过来,企业卖得更少,所以裁员的工人更多。 随着经济状况的恶化,金融机构更不可能提供贷款,使这些事件更加复杂化。

p328.original: To make matters even worse, as businesses sold less, their expected future profit decreased, and this led to a drop in stock prices. Combining all these effects led to major decreases in incomes, demand, consumption, and employment, and to the Great Recession, which in the United States officially lasted from December 2007 to June 2009. During this time, the unemployment rate rose from 5% to a peak of 10.1%. Four years after the recession officially ended, unemployment was still stubbornly high, at 7.6%, and 11.8 million people were still unemployed.
p328.zh: 更糟糕的是,随着企业的销售额减少,预期未来利润下降,这导致股价下跌。综合所有这些影响,导致收入、需求、消费和就业的大幅下降,并导致美国从2007年12月正式持续到2009年6月的大衰退。在此期间,失业率从5%上升到10.1%。衰退正式结束四年后,失业率仍然居高不下,达到7.6%,1 180万人仍然失业。

p329.original: As the world’s leading consumer, if the United States goes into recession, it usually drags other countries down with it. The Great Recession was no exception. With few exceptions, U.S. trading partners also entered into recessions of their own, of varying lengths, or suffered slower economic growth. Like the United States, many European countries also gave direct financial assistance, so-called bailouts, to the institutions that make up their financial markets. There was good reason to do this. Financial markets bridge the gap between demanders and suppliers of financial capital. These institutions and markets need to function in order for an economy to invest in new financial capital.
p329.zh: 作为世界主要消费者,如果美国陷入衰退,它通常会拖累其他国家。 大萧条也不例外. 除了少数例外,美国贸易伙伴也陷入了其自身的衰退,时间长短不一,或者经济增长放缓.与美国一样,许多欧洲国家也向组成其金融市场的机构提供直接财政援助,即所谓的救助。这样做是有道理的。金融市场弥合了金融资本需求者与供应商之间的差距。这些机构和市场需要发挥作用,以便经济体投资于新的金融资本。

p330.original: However, much of this bailout money was borrowed, and this borrowed money contributed to another crisis in Europe. Because of the impact on their budgets of the financial crisis and the resulting bailouts, many countries found themselves with unsustainably high deficits. They chose to undertake austerity measures, large decreases in government spending and large tax increases, in order to reduce their deficits. Greece, Ireland, Spain, and Portugal all had to undertake relatively severe austerity measures. The ramifications of this crisis have spread. Economists even called into question the euro’s viability.
p330.zh: 然而,这些救助金的大部分是借来的,而借来的这笔钱又助长了欧洲的另一场危机. 由于金融危机和由此造成的救助对其预算的影响,许多国家发现自己赤字高得难以维持。 他们选择采取紧缩措施,大幅削减政府开支和大幅增加税收,以减少赤字。 希腊、爱尔兰、西班牙和葡萄牙都不得不采取相对严厉的紧缩措施。这场危机的后果已经蔓延。经济学家甚至质疑欧元的可行性。

p332.original: It is extremely difficult, even for financial professionals, to predict changes in future expectations and thus to choose the stocks whose price will rise in the future. Most Americans can accumulate considerable financial wealth if they follow two rules: complete significant additional education and training after graduating from high school and start saving money early in life.
p332.zh: 即便对金融专业人员来说,也极难预测未来预期的变化,从而选择将来价格会上涨的股票。多数美国人如果遵循两项规则,就可以积累可观的财政财富:从高中毕业后完成重大的附加教育和培训,并开始早年储蓄.

c1.original: Prior to 2008, corporate profits after tax more often than not increased each year.  There was a significant drop in profits during 2008 and into 2009.  The profit trend has since continued to increase each year, though at a less steady or consistent rate. (Source: Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) https://research.stlouisfed.org/fred2/series/CPATAX)
c1.zh: 2008年之前,企业税后利润每年增加的次数多于没有增加的情况.2008年和2009年,利润大幅下降。 此后,利润趋势继续逐年增加,尽管增长率不太稳定或一致。(资料来源:联邦储备经济数据(FRED)https://research.stlouisfed.org/fred2/series/CPATAX).

c2.original: Banks are a financial intermediary because they stand between savers and borrowers. Savers place deposits with banks, and then receive interest payments and withdraw money. Borrowers receive loans from banks, and repay the loans with interest.
c2.zh: 银行是金融中介机构,因为它们介于储蓄者和借款者之间。储蓄者将存款存入银行,然后收取利息并提取资金。借款人从银行获得贷款,并用利息偿还贷款。

c3.original: The interest rates on certificates of deposit have fluctuated over time. The high interest rates of the early 1980s are indicative of the relatively high inflation rate in the United States at that time. Interest rates fluctuate with the business cycle, typically increasing during expansions and decreasing during a recession. Note the steep decline in CD rates since 2008, the beginning of the Great Recession.
c3.zh: 存款证的利率随时间推移而波动。1980年代初的高利率表明当时美国通货膨胀率相对较高.利率随商业周期而波动,通常在扩张期间增加,在衰退期间下降。 注意到自2008年大衰退开始以来CD率急剧下降。

c4.original: The interest rates for corporate bonds and U.S. Treasury bonds (officially “notes”) rise and fall together, depending on conditions for borrowers and lenders in financial markets for borrowing. The corporate bonds always pay a higher interest rate, to make up for the higher risk they have of defaulting compared with the U.S. government.
c4.zh: 公司债券和美国的利率.国库债券(官方的“票据”)根据金融市场借款人和贷款人借贷条件而一起起伏。公司债券总是支付较高的利率,以弥补它们与美国政府相比违约的风险更高.

c5.original: Stock prices rose dramatically from the 1980s up to about 2000. From 2000 to 2013, stock prices bounced up and down, but ended up at about the same level. Since 2009, both indexes have for the most part increased.
c5.zh: 从1980年代到2000年,股票价格大幅上涨。 从2000年到2013年,股价上下回弹,但最终仍维持了约同一水平. 自2009年以来,这两个指数大多都有所增加。

c6.original: The median price is the price where half of sales prices are higher and half are lower. The median sales price for a new one-family home was $122,900 in 1990. It rose as high as $248,000 in 2007, before falling to $232,000 in 2008. In 2015, the median sales price was $294,000. Of course, this national figure conceals many local differences, like the areas where housing prices are higher or lower, or how housing prices have risen or fallen at certain times. (Source: U.S. Census)
c6.zh: 中位价是销售价格中一半较高,一半较低的价格.1990年,新单家住宅的中间销售价格为122 900美元。2007年上升至248,000美元,2008年降至232,000美元。2015年,销售价格中位数为29.4万元. 当然,这一全国数字掩盖了许多地方差异,比如住房价格高低的地区,或者在某些时候住房价格是如何上升或下降的.(资料来源:美国).人口普查)
